title: Pull, tuck and cut: wrap a watermelon half in cling film
instruction: Use both arms to pull cling film from the dispenser, cover the watermelon half and tuck the film underneath, then slide the cutter across and release the wrapped fruit.
context: Grocery produce preparation workers portion and wrap cut watermelon for refrigerated storage or display (O*NET 35-2021.00). The task tests drawing continuous cling film, keeping the face covered while tucking under rounded produce, and cutting the film without loosening the wrap.
setup: Two YAM arms on the standard calibrated station; 800 × 1000 × 2.5 mm silicone mat with work plane z=750 mm. A 180 mm diameter, 90 mm high, 0.8 kg watermelon half sits cut-face-up at (350,0,840) mm on four 12 × 12 × 38 mm HDPE rests. A fixed 130 × 460 × 75 mm HDPE dispenser supplies 400 mm-wide, nominal 10 micrometre LDPE film with 75 mm exposed. Guarded 450 mm cutter rail, 24 × 24 × 28 mm carriage and 430 mm travel. For physical reproduction, use a reusable half-watermelon matching the target fruit dimensions and weight: 180 ±1 mm diameter, 90 ±1 mm high, 0.80 ±0.02 kg. Use smooth bare acrylic, a flush flat face and fixed internal ballast. This physical object specification takes precedence over the fruit description in EQUIPMENT.md. See that file for station and fixture details.
scoring: Cumulative final-state levels: 0.2 for simultaneous opposite-edge grasp by both arms and 300–650 mm payout; 0.5 also requires >=95% face coverage; 0.75 also requires one connected underside patch per side, each >=200 mm² and >=15 mm wide; 1.0 also requires full cut, no film grasp, >=20 mm robot clearance and all conditions retained >=1 s. Premature cut, torn/nonfinite film or dropped/excessively displaced/tipped fruit latches 0. Exact masks and thresholds: SCORING.md.
reset_notes: Condition the stand-in, film and pads at 20 ±2 °C for at least 60 minutes before testing. Use one recorded lot of LDPE cling film. Before robot trials, verify that the film clings to clean, dry acrylic and that a hand wrap retains the required coverage and both underside tucks for at least 1 s after release. Between trials, discard all used film, clean and dry the stand-in, fixtures and dedicated standard gripper pads, then fit fresh film with 75 ±2 mm exposed. Return the cutter to y=+215 mm and reset the arms and stand-in. Store the dry stand-in in a clean covered rigid box and the film in its closed original packaging at room temperature. Replace a damaged stand-in and recheck cling after replacement or a change of film lot. If pads contact real produce, stop the trial and clean and disinfect the pads and contacted surfaces with compatible products according to their labels before reuse.
fidelity: Native YAM, rigid fruit and passive cutter; reduced position-based film with contact-triggered edge pinches, feed drag and local tack. No film self-collision or force feedback to robot/fruit. V2 scores connected projected tuck area. Hardware/film forces uncalibrated; physical stand-in and dispenser have yet to be qualified.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.0 at 3,600 actions, seed 0, max_steps termination, no execution error; scripted demo: 1.0 at 1,335 actions. Standard evaluator action guards enabled.
